subject: Hosted API evaluation — sandbox access, rate expectations, and quick proof plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <acheng@brightcart.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation — sandbox access, rate expectations, and quick proof plan

Hi Alex — great demo yesterday, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the evaluation success criteria and avoid surprises when you exercise the sandbox: 

Key takeaways from the call
- BrightCart is validating a cart-assist generator and conversational product-help flow; initial traffic slice will be lower-latency but bursty (checkout spikes).
- Primary question: can hosted API meet latency targets while keeping unit cost reasonable vs a Dedicated pool?
- Compliance note: you mentioned SOC 2 scope later in procurement; that's a later-stage ask but flagged.

What we propose for a short proof plan (3 parts, 2 weeks):
1) Sandbox access + sample workload (2–3 days): we provision sandbox endpoints and a token scoped to your test workspace. You run representative traffic (we'll provide a small traffic driver) and log latency/throughput.
2) Endpoint profiling (3–4 days): our SRE run a profiling pass against your representative calls (sequence lengths, KV cache hit mix) and return an ops playbook (batching, prefix caching, quantization suggestions).
3) Ops check + decision checkpoint (remaining days): review results, map to deployment modes (Hosted baseline vs Dedicated recommendation) and agree next commercial step.

What I need from you to proceed:
- Confirm sandbox contact and preferred test window (timezone: PST).
- Baseline RPS and expected peak (e.g., 50 rps baseline, 300 rps peak for 10–15s bursts) — even estimates help.
- Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p95 targets).

Attachments: Redwood_Quickstart_Guide.pdf (quick steps for sandbox use) and BrightCart-Quickstart-Plan.xlsx (planning template).

Tentative availability for a 30-minute preflight call: Tue 4/20 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 4/21 14:00–15:00 PT. Let me know what works.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <acheng@brightcart.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@brightcart.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — sandbox access, rate expectations, and quick proof plan

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers below and one clarification: we want to start with Hosted if it meets latency and cost targets, but will need clear guidance on when we should move to Dedicated (expected > 1M requests/day or when average p95 exceeds 350ms).

Sandbox contact and window
- Primary: me (Alex Chen) — prefer Wed 4/21 morning PT.

Traffic profile (approx)
- Baseline: 20–30 rps steady for browsing-experiences.
- Checkout spikes: up to ~220 rps for short bursts (5–20s) during promos.
- Typical token lengths: prompts ~80–150 tokens; responses 40–120 tokens.

Latency targets
- Aim: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for the interactive flows (we can tolerate higher p95 for async recommendations).

Clarifying question
- For the sandbox: will we get a dedicated sandbox endpoint per customer or a shared sandbox with rate caps? We want to reproduce burst behavior without being throttled by unrelated tenants.

Also, procurement will ask for a sketch of expected costs if Hosted meets the SLA (monthly run-rate at these traffic levels). If you can include a rough run-rate estimate in the ops playbook that helps speed procurement.

Thanks — Alex
Product Lead, BrightCart

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — sandbox access, rate expectations, and quick proof plan

Alex — thanks for the quick responses, really helpful. Short answers + what we'll provision: 

Sandbox topology
- We'll provision a customer-scoped sandbox namespace (logical isolation) running on our hosted cluster. It's multi-tenant infra with per-customer rate ceilings; for your test window we'll increase the ceiling to reproduce bursts (we'll coordinate exact caps). So: shared infra + isolated namespace + adjustable test caps.

What we'll provision for Wed 4/21 (morning PT)
- Sandbox endpoints: https://sandbox.redwood.ai/brightcart/v1/generate (read-only test token; real key will be issued after the preflight)
- Temporary test ceiling: baseline 400 rps, burst headroom up to 600 rps for up to 30s windows (we'll monitor and adjust).
- Sample traffic driver + collection script (included in the Drive link) to capture p50/p95 and token counts.

Cost sketch (very rough)
- Using your profile (avg prompt+response ~200 tokens) and current Hosted unit cost bands, an order-of-magnitude monthly run-rate at steady 25 rps with occasional promoted bursts would land in the low five-figure range; sustained 200k–1M requests/month moves you toward Dedicated economics. We'll include a small cost model in the ops playbook tailored to the matrices you provided.

Preflight call
- Let's lock Wed 4/21 10:30 PT for the 30-min preflight. Jordan will run the ops checklist; Monica will own the cost model.

Next actions for BrightCart (short list)
- Confirm you can run the traffic driver in the morning window (we'll send the runner and a short README).
- Share any proxy/egress constraints or allowlist IPs for monitoring.
- Procurement: if you want a rough formal estimate for the Hosted commitment band, reply to this thread and Monica will attach a templated quote.

Attachments: Redwood_Quickstart_Guide.pdf (sandbox steps), BrightCart-Quickstart-Plan.xlsx (we'll prefill a few cells before Wed).

Thanks — looking forward.
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
